memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then you shall declare before the Lord your God: 'My father was a wandering Aramean, and he went down into Egypt with a few people and lived there and became a great nation, powerful and numerous.'" — Deut 26:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here the worshipper begins to tell his story — but it is not really his story at all. It is God's story of grace across generations. "My father was a wandering Aramean." He starts at the low point. His ancestor Jacob was a homeless wanderer, small and insignificant, who went down to Egypt with only a handful of people. And from that small, unpromising beginning, God made a great nation.

Isn't this how God so often works? He takes the small, the wandering, the overlooked, and He does something only He could do. Israel could take no credit for becoming a great nation. It was grace from start to finish.

Your story is like this too. If you belong to Christ, look back honestly at where you began — lost, wandering, far from God — and then look at what His grace has done. We were not saved because we were impressive. We were saved because God is merciful. The wanderer became a worshipper only because God reached down.

Never be ashamed of a humble beginning. God specialises in taking wandering people and giving them a home in His family (Eph 2:12-13). The lower the starting point, the clearer His grace shines.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can I trace God's grace across the story of my life?
2. Am I ever tempted to take credit for what only God has done?
3. How does remembering "where I began" deepen my gratitude?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Gracious God, I was once wandering and far from You, yet You brought me home. All that I am, I owe to Your mercy. Thank You for finding me. Amen.
